docRequirement: skills.md:635-663 binds us to a settings key spelled `skillOverrides`: a map whose key is a skill name and whose value is one of exactly four states — `"on"`, `"name-only"`, `"user-invocable-only"`, `"off"` — which "controls skill visibility from your settings instead of the skill's own frontmatter", for "skills whose SKILL.md you don't want to edit, such as ones checked into a shared project repo". The state table at :641-646 fixes the observable behaviour per state: `on` = name+description listed to the model, shown in the `/` menu; `name-only` = name listed without description, shown in the menu; `user-invocable-only` = hidden from the model, shown in the menu; `off` = hidden from both. :650 adds that as of v2.1.199 `"off"` also hides the skill from "the command lists advertised to Remote Control clients and to Agent SDK callers, not only the terminal `/` menu", and that "Invoking a hidden skill by its full name still returns the `skillOverrides` error instead of running it". :652 fixes the default: "A skill that is absent from `skillOverrides` is treated as `\"on\"`." :637 names the write destination `.claude/settings.local.json`. :663 exempts plugin skills entirely.
current: No reader of any spelling exists. `grep -ran skillOverrides` (with -a, so the repo's NUL-bearing files are not skipped) over `packages/` and `apps/` returns nothing; a case-insensitive sweep for `skilloverride`, `skill_override`, `skillvisibility`, `user-invocable-only`/`userInvocableOnly`, `name-only`/`nameOnly` finds no settings key of any spelling (the only `name-only` hits are unrelated MCP-allowlist prose and `packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:401`, which cites Claude's name-only state in a comment and does not implement it). What exists is the FRONTMATTER path only, in three consumers that all read one pinned handle: (1) the model-facing listing `PromptBuilder.buildSkillListingPart` at packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:403-447 filters solely on `skill.disableModelInvocation !== true` (:405) and always appends the description when the handle carries one (:430-432) — there is no name-only mode; (2) the `/` menu, `selectSkillSlashCommands` at packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:436-456, skips only `skill.userInvocable === false` (:443); (3) the invocation gate, `BaseAgent.resolveSkillReferences` at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2115-2155, refuses only on `runtimeSkill.disableModelInvocation === true` (:2141) and the `paths` scope check (:2148), and only for `origin === 'model'`. Both flags originate in SKILL.md frontmatter and nowhere else: packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:288-307 builds each skill record from `pinnedSkillMetadata(skillFile)`, resolver.ts:1659-1664 copies them onto `ResolvedCapability.skillDisableModelInvocation` / `.skillUserInvocable`, and packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:183-199 copies them onto `RuntimeSkillHandle.disableModelInvocation` / `.userInvocable`. No settings-side input reaches that chain: `resolver.ts:1595` derives a native record's `enabled` from `record.sourceEnabled`, and `sourceEnabled` is assigned at exactly one place, packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:594, from a Source's own `config.json` `enabled` field — skill records (native-sources.ts:288-307) never set it, so a native skill is unconditionally enabled. The only other native disable path, `sessionSelection.transientlyDisabledKeys` (resolver.ts:739, :1574, :1618, :2263), is transient by design and has no producer outside resolver.ts. The settings layer has the right shape and the wrong contents: packages/shared/src/config/bundled-skills-settings.ts is the exact precedent — a named key constant (`DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS_SETTING_KEY = 'disableBundledSkills'`, :58) plus a `(config: unknown) => …` reader (:84-87) applied in packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:667-693, where one memoized `readStoredConfig()` (:669-675) already gates the `discoveredRecords` filter that drops skill records (:687-693). Nothing analogous exists for per-skill visibility. `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` ARE read (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1051-1059) but only as `kind: 'permission'` records whose `permissions` block `claudeSettingsPermissionDsl` compiles (packages/shared/src/agent/permissions-config.ts:419-423, :511-529); every other key in those files is ignored. The sibling subsystem is implemented and is not a substitute: PLUGIN capabilities have a persisted, scoped enable/disable via `setCapabilityEnabled` (packages/shared/src/plugins/management-service-v2.ts:283-295) over `CapabilityPolicyStore`, whose `PolicyTarget` is `{pluginKey?, pluginInstanceId?}` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts:82-85) and therefore cannot address a native SKILL.md — and skills.md:663 exempts plugin skills from `skillOverrides` anyway.
divergence: The whole mechanism is absent, not merely renamed or narrowed. Three specific deltas: (1) There is no settings key of any spelling that reaches skill visibility — the four states, the absent-means-`on` default and the `.claude/settings.local.json` destination all have no implementation. (2) Two of the four states have no expressible equivalent even by hand: `user-invocable-only` maps onto the existing `disable-model-invocation: true`, and `off` onto `disable-model-invocation: true` + `user-invocable: false`, but both require editing the SKILL.md the doc sentence exists to avoid editing; `name-only` has no equivalent at all, because `buildSkillListingPart` (prompt-builder.ts:430-432) has no path that emits a listing line without the description. (3) The `"off"` invocation refusal is absent: `resolveSkillReferences` (base-agent.ts:2141-2151) refuses only on the frontmatter flag and only for `origin === 'model'`, so nothing can return the `skillOverrides` error, and a user typing the skill's full name is never refused at all. Scope note: the `"off"` hide-from-command-lists clause collapses to ONE surface here, not two — `SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16016-16048, skills at :16038) is served over the single RPC `workspace.ts:78` to the Electron renderer and to every remote websocket client alike.

userImpact: Concrete and reachable today. Clone a repo that ships skills at `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` or `.nessy-agent/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, open it as a project, and there is no way to hide or narrow any of them without changing the repository. In the Skills list the row's only actions are Show in Finder and a Delete that is greyed out and labelled "managed by project" (SkillsListPanel.tsx:69 requires `origin === 'native' && scope.kind === 'workspace' && !readOnly` to enable it; label at :95), and neither that row nor SkillInfoPage.tsx carries any enable/disable or visibility control. Meanwhile every one of those skills keeps its full name+description line in the model's `<available_skills>` block (prompt-builder.ts:403-447) — which is budget-capped, so on a repo with many skills the unwanted ones push wanted ones past `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS` and the model is told "(N more skills not listed — ask the user which to use.)" (:441-444); keeps a `/slug` entry in the composer's slash menu (SessionManager.ts:16038 → RPC workspace.ts:78); and stays invocable by the model. The user's only three levers are committing a frontmatter edit into someone else's repo, deleting the directory on disk, or refusing project trust — which is all-or-nothing for the project, not per skill.
